title: Jacobs Meister Röstung vs Cafèt Röstkaffee Gold
summary: Both are ground roast coffee in a 500 g pack, sold at the same chain.
evidence: Open Prices shows Jacobs Meister Röstung at 8.49 at Netto Marken-Discount in Berlin on 12 Aug 2026 and Cafèt Gold at 5.49 at Netto Marken-Discount in Villingen-Schwenningen on 12 Sep 2026. Pack sizes are from the Open Food Facts records.
differences: Cafèt lists an arabica and robusta blend. The Jacobs record gives no blend, so we can't compare them. We have no taste test for this pair.
why: Same chain, same form and same 500 g pack, and the Cafèt pack costs €3.00 less. One pack is enough to find out whether you like the blend.

title: Barilla Fusilli vs Combino Fusilli
summary: Both are dried durum wheat fusilli in a 500 g bag.
evidence: Open Prices shows Barilla Fusilli at 1.99 at Kaufland in Berlin on 25 Aug 2026 and Combino Fusilli at 0.69 at Lidl in Berlin on 22 Aug 2026. The two prices are from different chains.
differences: Combino's label warns of possible traces of egg and soy. Barilla pasta can be much cheaper on some days: Barilla Rigatoni 500 g was recorded at 0.88 at REWE in Jena in September 2026. We have no cooking or taste test for this pair.
why: The labels list the same main ingredient, durum wheat semolina, and the shape and bag size match. The Combino bag costs €1.30 less at these prices.

Ben's is often on offer: it was 1.49 at Netto in Strausberg in July 2026, about €6.77 per kg against €4.76 for K-Classic. We have no taste test for this pair.
why: Both are the same kind of quick pouch with rice, tomato, sunflower oil and basil on the label. K-Classic's pouch is bigger and cheaper, even when Ben's is on offer.

title: Oro di Parma Tomaten stückig vs ja! Tomaten gehackt

brand.product: Oro di Parma Tomaten stückig, 400 g

differences: Oro di Parma adds salt, ja! doesn't list it. ja! states 60% tomatoes plus juice, and the Oro di Parma record gives no percentage, so we can't say which has more tomato. We have no taste test for this pair.
why: For a sauce base, both tins hold chopped tomatoes with almost nothing else. The ja! tin costs €1.40 less.

title: Bonne Maman Aprikose vs Gut & Günstig Aprikose Konfitüre Extra

differences: Gut & Günstig states 50% apricots. The Bonne Maman record gives no fruit share and adds brown cane sugar. The two prices are six months apart. We have no taste test for this pair.
why: The ingredient lists nearly match, and Gut & Günstig is sold in a bigger jar at a lower price. Even against Bonne Maman's offer price it costs about half as much per 100 g.

title: Coca-Cola Original vs ja! Cola

evidence: Open Prices shows Coca-Cola 1.25 l at 1.59 at PENNY in Berlin on 6 Aug 2026 and at Netto in Berlin on 17 Jul 2026, and ja! Cola 1.5 l at 0.65 at REWE in Berlin on 20 Jul 2026. The labels are from Open Food Facts.
differences: Neither label gives the flavour recipe, so they may taste different, and we have no taste test for this pair. Bottle deposit comes on top of both prices.
why: The two labels list water, sugar, carbonation, caramel colour, phosphoric acid, flavouring and caffeine flavouring. Per litre ja! costs about a third of Coca-Cola, so a bottle is a cheap way to test it.

title: De Beukelaer Prinzenrolle Schoko vs ja! Doppelkeks
summary: Both are cocoa cream sandwich biscuits in a roll, with almost the same ingredient list.
evidence: Open Prices shows Prinzenrolle at 2.59 at Netto Marken-Discount in Strausberg on 11 Jul 2026. ja! Doppelkeks was 1.69 at HIT in Wiesbaden on 4 Nov 2026, and a second ja! Doppelkeks barcode was 1.69 at REWE Stenten in Aachen on 30 Oct 2026. The two brands' prices are from different chains.
differences: Prinzenrolle adds 2.3% dark chocolate, which ja! doesn't list. Prinzenrolle goes on offer: it was 2.29 at Netto in Strausberg in March 2026, still dearer per kilo than ja!. We have no taste test for this pair.
why: Flour, sugar, palm fat, starch and 5.5% cocoa powder appear on both labels in the same order. You get a bigger roll of ja! for 90 cents less, and the main recipe gap is a little dark chocolate.

title: Pringles Original vs Clarkys Stapelchips Original
summary: Both are stackable potato crisps in a tube, sold at the same chain.
evidence: Open Prices shows Pringles Original at 2.79 at Netto Marken-Discount in Berlin on 12 Aug 2026 and at Lidl in Berlin on 8 Aug 2026, and Clarkys Original at 1.49 at Netto Marken-Discount in Strausberg on 14 Oct 2026.
differences: The recipes differ: Pringles adds maize, wheat and rice flour, and Clarkys uses potato starch and a rapeseed oil mix. Clarkys comes 10 g lighter. Pringles was 2.49 at Rossmann in Bollensdorf in May 2026, which cuts the saving to about 37%. We have no taste test for this pair.
why: It's the same stacked crisp in the same kind of tube at the same chain, and Clarkys costs about 44% less per gram.

title: Doritos Nacho Cheese vs Clarkys Tortilla Chips Nacho Cheese

alternative.product: Clarkys Tortilla Chips Nacho Cheese (Netto), 300 g

differences: The seasoning differs. Doritos lists whey, buttermilk and cheese powders and a flavour enhancer, while Clarkys lists 1% cheese powder and no enhancer in what we could read, so the flavour may differ. We have no taste test for this pair.
why: For a bowl on the table it's the same maize chip with a nacho-cheese coating. The Clarkys bag is nearly three times the size and costs 80 cents less.

title: Iglo 15 Fischstäbchen vs Sea Gold Fischstäbchen

differences: Iglo goes on offer: it was 2.49 at a Netto in Strausberg on 23 Oct 2026, the same as Sea Gold, so at that price there's nothing to save. The breadcrumb recipes differ slightly. We have no taste test for this pair.

title: Kerrygold Irische Butter vs frija Irische Butter

key_ingredients.name: Lightly soured butter from Irish milk

summary: Both are lightly soured Irish butter in a 250 g block.
evidence: Open Prices shows Kerrygold at a regular 3.49 at EDEKA Woltersdorf on 16 Jun 2026 and at REWE in Dresden on 27 Mar 2026, and frija at 1.89 at a store recorded as Netto in Strausberg on 16 Jul 2026.
differences: This only pays when Kerrygold isn't on offer. It was 1.59 at EDEKA in Hamburg on 28 Oct 2026 and 1.79 at a Netto in Strausberg on 27 Aug 2026, both below frija's price, and our latest regular Kerrygold price is from June. Germany has two chains called Netto, so check both for frija. We have no taste test for this pair.
why: Both blocks are lightly soured Irish butter, so at the regular price there's little reason to pay €1.60 more. If Kerrygold is on offer below frija, buy Kerrygold.

title: Weihenstephan Haltbare Milch 1,5% vs Gut & Günstig H-Milch 1,5%
summary: Both are long-life milk with 1.5% fat in a 1 litre carton, priced at the same store.
evidence: Open Prices shows Weihenstephan at 1.49 at Feneberg in Kempten on 11 Sep 2026 and Gut & Günstig at 0.85 at Feneberg in Kempten on 7 Aug 2026. Weihenstephan was also 1.49 at V-MARKT in Mariaberg on 20 Jul 2026.
differences: Weihenstephan is often on offer: 0.99 at a Netto in Strausberg on 1 Sep 2026 and at V-MARKT on 8 Aug 2026, and a record of 1.11 at Aldi in Berlin. At 0.99 the saving is about 14%. Neither record gives processing details beyond UHT. We have no taste test for this pair.
why: Same fat level, same litre carton, same store, and milk is the only thing on the label. At the regular price Gut & Günstig costs 64 cents less per litre.

title: Philadelphia Original vs ja! Cremiger Frischkäse
summary: Both are plain full-fat cream cheese of the Doppelrahmstufe grade, seen at REWE stores.
evidence: Open Prices shows Philadelphia at 2.29 at REWE City in Köln on 29 Nov 2025 and ja! at 1.59 at REWE Stenten in Aachen on 25 Sep 2026. The 195 g size is on the tub in the Open Food Facts photo. The two prices are ten months apart.
differences: Philadelphia is named a cream cheese preparation and lists whey products, guar gum and citric acid, while ja! lists only cream cheese and salt. So the texture may differ. Flavoured Philadelphia tubs of 175 g were on offer at 1.29 at a Netto in March 2026, which is still dearer per kilo. We have no taste test for this pair.
why: Both are labelled Doppelrahmstufe, and the ja! tub has the shorter ingredient list. It's bigger and costs 70 cents less.

title: Milka Haselnusscreme vs Nussetti Nuss-Nougat-Creme
summary: Both are sweet hazelnut and cocoa spreads, priced at the same store on the same day.
evidence: Open Prices shows Milka Haselnusscreme at 3.79 for 350 g and Nussetti at 1.99 for 400 g, both at Netto Marken-Discount in Strausberg on 2 Nov 2026. Milka was 3.69 at Kaufland in Strausberg on 19 Mar 2026.
differences: Milka uses sunflower oil and Nussetti uses rapeseed and palm oil, so if you avoid palm oil, Milka wins. Nussetti lists 13% hazelnuts against 5% hazelnut mass in Milka. Milka lists its cocoa after that 5%, so it has 5% or less, against 9% in Nussetti. We have no taste test for this pair.
why: The Nussetti label shows more hazelnut and more cocoa, in a bigger jar, for €1.80 less. Unless you're avoiding palm oil, the label gives little reason to pay more.

title: Monster Energy Zero Sugar vs Speedstar Energydrink Ultra Zero
summary: Both are sugar-free energy drinks in a 500 ml can, listing the same levels of caffeine, taurine, ginseng and guarana.
evidence: Open Prices shows Monster Energy Zero Sugar at 1.49 at Lidl in Berlin on 8 Aug 2026 and Speedstar Ultra Zero at 0.69 at Norma in Ludwigshafen on 25 Aug 2026. The percentages are from the labels on Open Food Facts. The two prices are from different chains.
differences: The flavours and colours aren't the same recipe, and Monster also lists erythritol. Monster flavours go on offer: Ultra Fiesta Mango was 0.77 at Netto Marken-Discount in Berlin in July 2026, close to Speedstar's price. Can deposit comes on top of both prices. We have no taste test for this pair.
why: The active ingredients on the two labels match at the percentages stated. Speedstar costs 80 cents less per can, which is less than half the price.

title: Löwensenf Extra vs Bautz'ner Senf scharf
summary: Both are hot German table mustards made from mustard seed, vinegar, water and salt.
evidence: Open Prices shows Löwensenf Extra at 1.89 at EDEKA Y. Reichelt in Berlin on 3 Aug 2026 and Bautz'ner scharf at a regular 0.55 at Netto in Berlin on 20 Jul 2026. The two prices are from different chains.
differences: Löwensenf is sold as extra hot and Bautz'ner as hot, so the heat may differ, and we have no test for this pair. Bautz'ner adds sugar, paprika and spices, while Löwensenf lists none. Löwensenf comes in a 250 ml jar and Bautz'ner in a 200 ml tub.
why: Mustard is a small part of any meal, and both are made from seed, vinegar, water and salt. Per litre Bautz'ner costs about a third as much.

title: Heinz Tomato Ketchup vs Le Gusto Tomato Ketchup
summary: Both are plain tomato ketchup in a squeeze bottle, with the price per litre far apart.
evidence: Open Prices shows Heinz at a regular 2.79 at Lidl in Bach on 21 Feb 2026, and Le Gusto at 1.29 at Aldi in Strausberg on 8 Apr 2026. On that same day at that Aldi, Heinz was on offer at 1.79.
differences: Heinz states 148 g of tomatoes per 100 g of ketchup. The Le Gusto ingredient list on file is unreadable, so we can't compare tomato share, and Heinz may use more. Germany has two Aldi chains and the record doesn't say which sold Le Gusto, so check both. We have no taste test for this pair.
why: Even on offer at the same Aldi, Heinz works out at about €4.48 per litre against €2.58 for Le Gusto. Try one bottle and see whether you can tell them apart.

title: Thomy Delikatess Mayo vs ja! Mayonnaise

title: Thomy Reines Sonnenblumenöl vs Vegola Sonnenblumenöl

why: A single-ingredient oil gives little room for a difference on the label. The Vegola bottle is a third bigger and still costs €1.10 less.

title: Bonduelle Goldmais vs Kaufland Gemüse Mais

why: It's a single-ingredient snack, so there's little on the label to set them apart. Kaufland's bag holds 50 g more and costs about 35% less per gram.

title: Listerine Cool Mint Mild vs Dontodent Mundspülung
summary: Both are daily mouth rinses with sodium fluoride and no alcohol on the label, in a 500 ml bottle, seen at dm.
evidence: Open Prices shows Listerine Cool Mint Mild at 3.95 at dm in Berlin on 20 Aug 2026, with similar prices at Kaufland and Netto Marken-Discount that month, and Dontodent at 0.85 at dm in Barsinghausen on 7 Jan 2026. Ingredients are from the Open Food Facts records. The two prices are seven months apart.
differences: The antibacterial ingredients aren't the same: Listerine uses essential oil compounds and Dontodent uses cetylpyridinium chloride. We have no test of Dontodent or any test comparing the two, so we can't say they work equally well. Listerine was 2.99 at REWE in Berlin on 25 Aug 2026. Ask a dentist if you use a rinse for a gum problem.
why: For a daily rinse with fluoride, Dontodent costs about a fifth of the price. If a dentist told you to use Listerine, stay with it, because the antibacterial ingredients differ.

title: Fairy Konzentrat vs Shine Spülmittel Konzentrat

alternative.product: Shine Washing-up Liquid Concentrated Classic (Netto), 500 ml

summary: Both are concentrated hand washing-up liquids, priced at one store on one day.
evidence: Open Prices shows Fairy at 1.69 for 450 ml and Shine at 1.25 for 500 ml, both at a store recorded as Netto in Strausberg on 13 Feb 2026. Open Prices' product records give the sizes.
differences: Neither ingredient list is on file, so we can't compare how concentrated they are, and you may need more or less of one per wash. We found no cleaning test that covers Shine. Germany has two chains called Netto, so check both for Shine.
why: Both are sold as concentrates, and Shine comes out about a third cheaper per millilitre. Check how far a squeeze goes before you buy it in quantity.
